transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m here because I just feel completely drained. Like, even walking from my car into the clinic took a lot out of me, and at work, just opening the EHR feels like it takes everything I have.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I have. After my energy kind of crashed, I started feeling empty most days. Just really hopeless, like I already messed up my future in healthcare before I even really got started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying much attention to that, honestly. I know I feel worn out and low, but I don’t know if it’s that I don’t enjoy things or just that I don’t have the energy for them.
Have you been sleeping more than usual, less than usual, or about the same?

It’s been kind of all over. For a while I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours and still felt wired, like I didn’t need more. But lately it’s the opposite sometimes—I wake up before dawn sick with worry, or I sleep half the day and still feel exhausted.
During the times when you slept only two or three hours and still felt wired, did you also feel unusually up, euphoric, or more irritable than usual?

Yeah. Some days I felt really good, like amazing, like I could handle anything and nothing could stop me. But then if somebody corrected my documentation or told me to slow down, I’d get really irritated and snap at them, like they were insulting me.
During those times when you felt amazing and only needed a few hours of sleep, did you find yourself taking on a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I started making all these new workflow plans and sending messages to coworkers after hours. I was offering to train people even when I was barely ahead of them myself. I kept taking on extra tasks, and then it got to the point where I couldn’t even finish the basic stuff safely.
During those times when you felt amazing, did you feel more confident or important than usual?

Yeah… I did. I felt like I knew better than the nurses and even the managers about how patient care should be done. At the time I really believed if they just listened to me, I could fix things and change the whole system.
During those times when you felt amazing and hardly needed sleep, did you ever hear or see things that other people didn’t?

Yeah… mostly hearing things. During shifts I’d hear my name over the clinic speaker, or I’d hear a monitor beeping like it was for me, but nobody else seemed to hear it. I’d end up going to look for a patient who wasn’t actually calling.
During those high-energy periods, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your life?

Yes. It got serious at work. I couldn’t keep up with the basic documentation, and I didn’t feel safe trying to focus on patient-support tasks. Employee health ended up pulling me from work and sending me for an emergency evaluation. I also had to stop really preparing for my CNA certification because I just couldn’t keep up.
When you heard your name over the speaker or a monitor beeping for you, did you believe at the time that it was really happening?

Yes. At the time I really thought it was happening. Like if I heard my name over the speaker or a monitor going off, I believed it was for me, and I’d go looking for the patient or the reason for it. It wasn’t until later that I realized nobody else had heard it.
